name: Butter Chicken
description: Tandoori chicken simmered in a tomato-butter gravy — a Delhi-Punjab restaurant classic.

steps.instruction: Marinate chicken in yogurt, ginger-garlic, chilli, and salt for at least 30 minutes.
Grill or pan-sear until lightly charred.
Cook tomato puree with butter, kasuri methi, and spices until thick.
Add chicken and cream; simmer 10 minutes and finish with a knob of butter.

name: Amritsari Kulcha
description: Leavened stuffed bread baked in a tandoor, eaten with chole in Amritsar.

steps.instruction: Knead a soft dough with flour, yogurt, oil, and a pinch of baking soda.
Stuff with spiced mashed potato, onion, and coriander.
Roll, brush with ghee, and bake until blistered.

name: Chole Bhature
description: Spiced chickpea curry with puffed fried bread, a north Indian breakfast staple.

steps.instruction: Soak and boil chickpeas; cook in onion-tomato masala with chole spice.
Ferment a yogurt dough, roll discs, and deep-fry until they balloon.

name: Rogan Josh
description: Kashmiri lamb curry coloured with ratan jot or Kashmiri chilli, fragrant with fennel and ginger.

steps.instruction: Brown lamb in ghee with whole spices.
Stir in yogurt off the heat so it does not split.
Add chilli, fennel, and ginger; slow-cook until the meat is tender.

name: Yakhni Pulao
description: Aromatic rice cooked in a mild yogurt-mutton stock, a Kashmiri festive pulao.

steps.instruction: Simmer mutton with whole spices to make yakhni stock.
Cook soaked rice in the strained stock until fluffy.

name: Kashmiri Dum Aloo
description: Baby potatoes in a yogurt-chilli gravy without onion or garlic, in the Kashmiri pandit style.

steps.instruction: Prick, fry, or bake baby potatoes until golden.
Cook yogurt gravy with chilli, fennel, and ginger; add potatoes and dum-cook.

name: Dal Baati Churma
description: Baked wheat baatis served with panchmel dal and sweet crushed churma — Rajasthan's signature thali.

steps.instruction: Shape stiff wheat dough into baatis and bake until cracked and brown.
Soak hot baatis in ghee; serve with spicy mixed dal and sweet churma.

name: Laal Maas
description: Fiery mutton curry of Mathania chillies from the Thar, traditionally cooked in a pot over wood.

name: Ghevar
description: Disc-shaped honeycomb sweet soaked in sugar syrup, made for Teej and Raksha Bandhan.

name: Lucknowi Biryani
description: Awadhi pakki/kacchi layered rice and marinated meat steamed under a sealed dough lid.

steps.instruction: Marinate meat with yogurt and whole spices.
Parboil fragrant basmati; layer with meat and saffron.
Seal the pot and dum-cook on low heat until steam-cooked through.

name: Galouti Kebab
description: Melt-in-the-mouth minced meat kebabs invented in Lucknow for a toothless Nawab.

name: Varanasi Pedha
description: Milk-solid sweet of the Banaras tradition, often offered as prasad.

name: Litti Chokha
description: Roasted sattu-stuffed wheat balls with mashed spiced potato, eggplant, and tomato.

name: Sattu Paratha
description: Whole-wheat flatbread stuffed with spiced roasted gram flour, a Bihar staple.

name: Rasgulla
description: Chhena balls simmered in light sugar syrup — a Bengali (and Odia) celebration sweet.

name: Kosha Mangsho
description: Slow-bhuna mutton of Bengal, dark, thick, and served with luchis or rice.

name: Shorshe Ilish
description: Hilsa in a pungent mustard-poppy gravy, the monsoon pride of Bengal.

name: Sandesh
description: Delicate chhena sweet often flavoured with nolen gur in winter.

name: Dalma
description: Toor dal cooked with native vegetables and tempered with ghee and cumin — temple-style Odia comfort food.

name: Chhena Poda
description: Baked caramelised chhena cake, Odisha's signature roasted cheese sweet.

name: Masala Dosa
description: Crisp fermented rice-lentil crepe filled with spiced potato, served with chutney and sambar.

steps.instruction: Spread fermented batter thin on a hot tava.
Add potato masala, fold, and serve with coconut chutney and sambar.

name: Bisi Bele Bath
description: Hot lentil-rice with vegetables and a distinctive spice blend from Karnataka.

name: Mysore Pak
description: Ghee-rich gram-flour fudge created in the Mysore palace kitchens.

name: Hyderabadi Biryani
description: Kacchi dum biryani of the Deccan: raw marinated meat layered with half-cooked rice.

name: Haleem
description: Slow-pounded Ramadan porridge of wheat, lentils, and meat, iconic in Hyderabad.

name: Appam with Vegetable Stew
description: Lacy fermented rice hoppers with a coconut-milk vegetable stew.

name: Kerala Fish Curry
description: Kudampuli or mango-sour fish curry in coconut, a Syrian Christian and coastal staple.

name: Puttu Kadala
description: Steamed rice-coconut cylinders served with black chickpea curry.

name: Avial
description: Coconut-yogurt mixed vegetable dish essential to the Onam sadya.

name: Chettinad Chicken
description: Pepper-fennel chicken of the Chettiar kitchens, roasted whole spices ground fresh.

name: Idli Sambar
description: Steamed rice-lentil cakes with a tamarind-lentil vegetable sambar.

name: Filter Coffee
description: Decoction coffee mixed with boiled milk and poured between tumbler and davara.

name: Vada Pav
description: Mumbai's street sandwich: spiced potato fritter in a pav with chutneys.

steps.instruction: Mash spiced potato, shape, dip in gram-flour batter, and fry.
Tuck into pav with garlic and green chutney.

name: Pav Bhaji
description: Mashed vegetable curry cooked on a tava, served with buttered pav.

name: Puran Poli
description: Festive flatbread stuffed with sweet chana dal and jaggery.

name: Misal Pav
description: Sprouted-bean curry with farsan and pav, a fiery Pune–Kolhapur breakfast.

name: Goan Fish Curry
description: Coconut-tamarind fish curry with Kashmiri chilli, eaten with rice.

name: Bebinca
description: Layered Indo-Portuguese coconut-egg pudding baked one sheet at a time.

name: Dhokla
description: Steamed fermented gram-flour cake tempered with mustard and curry leaf.

name: Thepla
description: Fenugreek flatbread that travels well — a Gujarati journey food.

name: Undhiyu
description: Winter mixed-vegetable casserole of Surat, traditionally cooked inverted in an earthen pot.

name: Indori Poha
description: Flattened rice with jeeravan masala, sev, and pomegranate — Indore's breakfast.

name: Jalebi
description: Fermented batter coils fried crisp and soaked in saffron syrup, eaten with poha in Indore.

name: Dal Bafla
description: Boiled-then-baked wheat dumplings with dal, Malwa's cousin of Rajasthani baati.

name: Thukpa
description: Himalayan noodle soup of the Tibetan-Sikkimese table, often with chicken or vegetables.

name: Momos
description: Steamed dumplings with spicy tomato-sesame chutney, ubiquitous across the eastern Himalaya.

name: Masor Tenga
description: Light sour fish curry with tomatoes or thekera, everyday Assamese food.

name: Til Pitha
description: Rice-flour pancake stuffed with sesame and jaggery, made at Magh Bihu.

name: Jadoh
description: Khasi red rice cooked with pork, a Meghalaya comfort dish.

name: Skyu
description: Thumb-pressed wheat pasta stew with root vegetables, a Ladakhi winter meal.
